items.title: Cerebras is serving trillion-parameter models
items.oneliner: Cerebras says Kimi K3 runs on 59 wafers. Trillion-parameter inference is becoming an infrastructure problem, not a research fantasy.

items.title: Block is betting on speech-to-speech AI
items.oneliner: Block's Dessa skips text and talks full duplex. Voice agents are moving from transcription pipelines to native conversation.

items.title: EPFL built a closed-loop neural chip
items.oneliner: EPFL's LogSync decodes cross-brain signals in real time. Adaptive neurostimulation is getting closer to software-defined psychiatry.

items.title: Brotli decoding became an RCE surface
items.oneliner: Broccoli2Shell turns malformed Brotli into RCE across Node.js, Python, and more. Compression libraries just joined your threat model.

items.title: The php2shell bug reached live targets
items.oneliner: Public exploitation of php2shell appeared three days after patches landed. Patch windows for internet-facing stacks are effectively gone.

items.title: Revoked certificates stayed live on government sites
items.oneliner: Indian government sites kept serving revoked eMudhra certificates days later. PKI failures are still operational failures, not paperwork.

items.title: POSIX wordexp remains a command injection trap
items.oneliner: wordexp(3) can still execute commands on untrusted input, even with safeguards. Legacy convenience APIs keep aging into liabilities.

items.title: Samsung device telemetry raised surveillance concerns
items.oneliner: Reports say Samsung devices scan nearby Bluetooth microphones and run on-device tracking models. Smart TV privacy is now an ML story.

items.title: A two-dollar chip ran real-time vision
items.oneliner: An ESP32-S3 ran SIMD-accelerated FAST detection in 6 ms at QVGA. Edge vision keeps getting cheaper than your cloud bill.

items.title: Farol scores pull request risk
items.oneliner: Farol maps pull request risk for reviewers instead of summarizing diffs. AI code review is finally inching toward triage.
